h02.task: group-level leave-one-device-out (device constant per subject -> no subject-level fold; 3 cameras x same protocol)
h02.classes: 2-class: normal (DG0, 278 series/2980 imgs) vs pathological (DG1-13, 206 series/15032 imgs); secondary: ROP stage [1,2,3,4] vs hemorrhage(DG11) vs other-path
h02.protocol: torchvision ResNet18 pretrained, 224px, weighted CE, per fold: train on 2 devices, test on held-out device; 3 folds + in-domain baseline (device D1 internal split seed42)
h02.decision: PASS if all 3 leave-one-device macro-F1 >= 0.85 AND worst cross-device F1 >= worst in-domain F1 - 0.10; otherwise FAIL/MEASURE (gap quantification is the primary output)
h02.data_note: 6004 unique images from 04-data/raw/extracted/images; labels from filenames (DG code); CSV is series-level (484 series) not image-level

result.interpretation: Plain pretrained ResNet18 (2-class normal vs pathological, group-level 3-fold) generalizes in-domain (0.88) but cross-device drops to 0.56-0.63 (gap ~0.30 macro-F1). The 3 infant-fundus cameras (RetCam3/RetCam Envision/Phoenix ICON) impose a real, large imaging domain shift that a fixed backbone does NOT bridge. This is the primary output for the #77 multi-device imaging domain-adaptation family: domain adaptation is NECESSARY (not trivially solved by pretrained features), justifying a leave-one-device-out domain-adaptation baseline + per-camera feature-distribution quantification as the paper contribution. Cross-domain asymmetry note: D3 (Phoenix ICON, only 974 imgs) hardest as both train- and test-holdout.
